ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Ada Lovelace

code.originalText: Fourteen-week review: restaging CT, blood counts, iron and thyroid, pain, and a goals-of-care conversation

text.paragraph: Fourteen-week review after four cycles: restaging CT, blood counts, iron and thyroid, pain, and goals of care. [S]

Mrs. Lovelace returns a week after her fourth cycle. The restaging CT a week ago shows a partial response. She has had no bleeding. Her average pain is 3 of 10 on long-acting morphine 15 mg twice a day, now with a breakthrough dose only once or twice a week. She has mild tingling in her toes that does not affect walking or buttons. She tires for three or four days after each cycle. Her bowels are regular on the laxatives. She has no rash, diarrhea, cough, or cold intolerance. She is working most mornings. She has stopped betting and is meeting the social worker about her debts. The thyroid test due six weeks into treatment and the ferritin due after the iron infusions were not drawn; both were drawn today. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-08; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well, not sedated; blood pressure 112/70, pulse 80, weight 54.0 kg
Light touch slightly reduced at the toes; vibration and strength normal; grade 1 neuropathy

Bleeding between periods and after intercourse, with heavier periods, a watery blood-stained discharge and a constant pelvic ache, for about five months; average pain 7 of 10 despite her opium tincture; a friable cervical mass found on examination and biopsied; cause not yet established at intake
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented final illness; superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 74 fL, ferritin 5 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs
S — Synthetic modern finding anchored to her documented final illness.

Adenocarcinoma of the endocervix, usual (HPV-associated) type, HPV 18 positive, FIGO 2018 stage IVB: a 5.2 cm tumor with left parametrial invasion, metastases to left pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes, and bilateral lung metastases on MRI and PET-CT; PD-L1 combined positive score 5, mismatch repair proficient, HER2 1+; treated with palliative pelvic radiation for bleeding and carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab, with specialist palliative care from diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit, anchored to her documented uterine cancer; the cervical site is a synthetic choice.
Cancer-related pelvic pain, nociceptive and visceral, from the cervical tumor and its left parametrial extension
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit.

Long-term prescribed opioid therapy: opium tincture for recurrent pelvic and abdominal pain for about two years, measured at times with a household spoon, converted at intake to measured oral morphine; no opioid use disorder on a DSM-5 assessment; naloxone supplied
S — Synthetic modern history anchored to her documented laudanum and opium; not a claim about her real dosing.

Drug-induced constipation from long-acting morphine and ondansetron, a week after the first chemotherapy cycle: no bowel movement for five days, with bloating and cramping but passing wind, without vomiting; no bowel obstruction on examination; potassium and calcium normal; resolved with laxatives
S — Synthetic adverse drug effect; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Metastatic cervical adenocarcinoma, partial response (C53.0). CT after four cycles shows a partial response: the cervical tumor 3.1 cm, lung nodules smaller and two gone, para-aortic nodes below 1 cm, no new lesions. Counts allow treatment: white cells 3.8, neutrophils 1.9, platelets 172; creatinine 0.72 mg/dL, ALT 26 U/L. TSH 3.4 mIU/L. Grade 1 neuropathy does not need a dose change. [S]
Complete six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel, then continue pembrolizumab every 3 weeks.
Restaging CT about three months after this one.
Report any worsening numbness, which would lead to a paclitaxel dose reduction.

Iron deficiency anemia, iron replete (D50.0). Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL without bleeding; ferritin 210 ng/mL, so iron stores are replete; the remaining anemia is from chemotherapy. [S]
No further iron; blood count with each cycle.

Cancer-related pelvic pain, controlled (G89.3). Average 3 of 10 with few breakthrough doses. [S]
Continue the current doses; consider tapering if pain stays low after chemotherapy.

Goals of care. Goals-of-care conversation with Mrs. Lovelace, with the palliative care physician present. She understands that the cancer is responding but cannot be cured. Her hopes are to keep working on her mathematics and to stay at home; her fears are pain and losing her clarity of mind. She wants to continue treatment while it allows that, and she chose not to have resuscitation attempted if her heart stops, while keeping all other treatment. A portable medical order was completed. [S]
Share the order with the oncology and palliative care teams.
Revisit at each restaging.

Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, white cells 3.8, neutrophils 1.9, platelets 172
TSH and free T4 on pembrolizumab

TSH 3.4 mIU/L. Protocol deviation: the TSH and free T4 due six weeks after baseline were not drawn, because they were left to be added to the cycle 3 blood tests and were not ordered; drawn today, twelve weeks after baseline. No harm resulted: TSH is normal and she has no thyroid symptoms. Corrective action: a standing order for TSH and free T4 every six weeks while she takes pembrolizumab

Ferritin 210 ng/mL. Protocol deviation: the ferritin due 6 to 8 weeks after the second infusion was not drawn at the preventive visit, which fell in that window; drawn today, twelve weeks after. No harm resulted: stores are replete and hemoglobin is rising. Corrective action: list post-infusion tests on the problem list with their due dates
